```python
def trigger_emotional_intervention(user_id, real_time_metrics, historical_data):
    """
    Decide which emotional‑support intervention (if any) to deploy for the given learner.
    Returns a dict: { "intervention": <type>, "payload": <details> } or None.
    """

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Normalise / unpack the real‑time signals
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    typing_speed      = real_time_metrics.get('typing_speed')      # chars/sec
    voice_pitch       = real_time_metrics.get('voice_pitch')       # Hz (optional)
    sentiment_score   = real_time_metrics.get('sentiment_score')   # –1 (negative) … +1 (positive)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Pull a few key historical aggregates (cached per user)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    #   • avg_sentiment_last_30min   – rolling mean of sentiment scores
    #   • avg_typing_speed_last_30min
    #   • last_intervention_ts        – when we last intervened
```

```python
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Focus Guardian – Detect & Neutralise External‑Help‑Seeking Behaviour
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Input shapes (simplified – adapt to your data model):
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#   user_id               : str / int
#   activity_data         : dict {
#        "alt_tab_count"          : int          # # of times the OS window focus changed in last N seconds
#        "new_browser_tab_url"    : str | None   # full URL of any freshly‑opened tab (or None)
#        "clipboard_content"       : str | None   # raw text that was just copied
#   }
#   tutor_state           : dict {
#        "last_intervention_ts"   : datetime | None   # when we last showed a Focus‑Guardian cue
#        "current_question_id"    : str               # identifier of the problem the learner is working on
#        "question_text"          : str               # full canonical text of the problem (cleaned)
#        "session_start_ts"       : datetime
#        "emotion_state"         : dict { "stress_score":float, "sentiment_score":float }
#   }
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Return value (or None):
#   {
#        "intervention" : "scaffolding_hint" | "relatable_peer_invite",
#        "payload"      : dict   # ready‑to‑render UI data
#   }
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def intercept_external_help_seeking(user_id,
                                    activity_data,
                                    tutor_state):
    """
    Core of the Focus Guardian.  Detects early signals that the learner
    is about to look up the answer elsewhere and injects a helpful,
    in‑app intervention before they leave the flow.
    """

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 0️⃣  QUICK COOLDOWN – avoid spamming the same learner
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 90                         # min interval between two focus‑guardian cues
    now = utc_now()
    last_ts = tutor_state.get('last_intervention_ts')
    if last_ts and (now - last_ts).total_seconds() < COOLDOWN_SECONDS:
        return None                               # Too soon → let the learner continue

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  EXTRACT RAW signals
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    alt_tab_cnt   = activity_data.get('alt_tab_count', 0)
    new_url       = activity_data.get('new_browser_tab_url')
    clipboard_txt = activity_data.get('clipboard_content')

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  DEFINE heuristics that flag “external‑help‑seeking”
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    #   a) Frequent Alt‑Tabbing (window‑switching) – suggests the learner
    #      is searching for something else.
    #   b) Opening a *search‑engine* URL (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, etc.)
    #      within a few seconds of the current problem.
    #   c) Copy‑pasting the exact problem text (or a large chunk of it)
    #      to the clipboard – classic “copy‑and‑paste‑into‑Google” pattern.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------

    # ---------- a) Alt‑Tab heuristic ----------
    ALT_TAB_THRESHOLD = 3          # three switches in the monitoring window = suspicious
    alt_tab_flag = alt_tab_cnt >= ALT_TAB_THRESHOLD

    # ---------- b) URL heuristic ----------
    SEARCH_DOMAINS = {
        "google.com", "www.google.com",
        "bing.com", "www.bing.com",
        "duckduckgo.com", "www.duckduckgo.com",
        "yahoo.com", "search.yahoo.com"
    }

    url_flag = False
    if new_url:
        domain = extract_domain(new_url)          # strip protocol, path, query
        if domain.lower() in SEARCH_DOMAINS:
            # Optional: look for query terms that overlap with the problem keywords
            if contains_problem_keywords(new_url, tutor_state['question_text']):
                url_flag = True
            else:
                # Even without keyword overlap, opening a search engine is a strong signal
                url_flag = True

    # ---------- c) Clipboard heuristic ----------
    clipboard_flag = False
    if clipboard_txt:
        # Normalise both strings (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace)
        cleaned_clip = normalise_text(clipboard_txt)
        cleaned_prob = normalise_text(tutor_state['question_text'])

        # If the copied text contains > 70 % of the problem wording, we treat it as a copy‑paste action.
        overlap = jaccard_similarity(cleaned_clip, cleaned_prob)
        # Also treat very long clipboard snippets (> 150 chars) as a possible answer‑search attempt.
        if overlap >= 0.70 or len(cleaned_clip) > 150:
            clipboard_flag = True

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  COMBINE signals into a *risk score* (0‑1)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # We weight the three signals; feel free to tweak the constants.
    risk = (
        0.4 * (1 if alt_tab_flag else 0) +
        0.3 * (1 if url_flag else 0) +
        0.3 * (1 if clipboard_flag else 0)
    )
    # Clamp to [0,1] just in case
    risk = max(0.0, min(1.0, risk))

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Decide *what* intervention to deploy
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # If risk is low (< 0.3) → ignore.  If moderate (0.3‑0.6) → gentle scaffolding.
    # If high (≥0.6) → more emphatic offer of a relatable‑peer session.
    # An additional rule: if clipboard_flag is true, we *always* give a hint
    # because the learner has already exposed the problem text.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if risk < 0.30:
        return None               # No sign of external‑help seeking

    if clipboard_flag or risk >= 0.60:
        # High‑confidence or explicit copy‑paste → give a **Scaffolding Hint**
        # (the hint is context‑aware and delivered instantly)
        payload = {
            "hint_type"   : "step_by_step",
            "question_id" : tutor_state['current_question_id'],
            "message"     : generate_scaffold_hint(tutor_state['question_text'])
        }
        chosen_intervention = "scaffolding_hint"

            current_user_id=user_id,
            user_emotional_state=tutor_state.get('emotion_state', {}),
            peer_database=fetch_active_peers(limit=200)   # cached & fast
        )
        if peer_payload:
            payload = {
                "peer_id"     : peer_payload["peer_id"],
                "peer_name"   : peer_payload.get("peer_name"),
                "peer_pic"    : peer_payload.get("peer_pic"),
                "message"     : ("👥 Looks like you might need a fresh perspective. "
                                 "Would you like to see how {peer_name} tackled a similar problem?").format(
                                    peer_name=peer_payload["peer_id"]  # or display_name
                                )
            }
            chosen_intervention = "relatable_peer_invite"
        else:
            # Fallback to a generic motivational nudge if no peer is available
            payload = {
                "hint_type"   : "quick_tip",
                "message"     : "Take a deep breath – you’ve got the pieces, let’s put them together!"
            }
            chosen_intervention = "scaffolding_hint"

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Record the intervention (for cooldown & analytics)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    record_focus_guardian_intervention(
        user_id=user_id,
        timestamp=now,
        kind=chosen_intervention,
        risk_score=risk,
        raw_signals={
            "alt_tab": alt_tab_cnt,
            "url": new_url,
            "clipboard": bool(clipboard_txt)
        }
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6️⃣  Return the decision payload to the UI layer
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    return {
        "intervention": chosen_intervention,
        "payload"     : payload,
        "risk_score"  : risk
    }
```

## 2️⃣ Helper utilities (keep them pure & testable)

```python
def _similarity(user: EmotionalState, peer: PeerProfile) -> float:
    """
    Returns a similarity score (0‑1) based on:
      • demographic hash match (1.0 if exact, 0.5 if same country, 0 otherwise)
      • proximity of recent_score (Gaussian‑like decay)
      • overlap of curriculum_path (Jaccard index)
    """
    # 1️⃣ Demographic similarity
    demo_score = 1.0 if user["demographic_hash"] == peer["demographic_hash"] else 0.5

    # 2️⃣ Score proximity (σ ≈ 10 points gives a smooth curve)
    score_dist = abs(user["recent_score"] - peer["recent_score"])
    score_score = math.exp(- (score_dist ** 2) / (2 * (10 ** 2)))

    # 3️⃣ Path overlap
    user_path = set(user["curriculum_path"])
    peer_path = set(peer["curriculum_path"])
    if not user_path or not peer_path:
        path_score = 0.0
    else:
        path_score = len(user_path & peer_path) / len(user_path | peer_path)

    # Weighted blend (tune these weights experimentally)
    return 0.4 * demo_score + 0.4 * score_score + 0.2 * path_score


def _aspiration_score(user: EmotionalState, peer: PeerProfile) -> float:
    """
    Higher when the peer is *ahead* but still reachable.
    """
    # Must be ahead on mastery (≥ 10 pts) but not absurdly far (> 40 pts)
    mastery_gap = peer["mastery"] - user["mastery"]
    if mastery_gap < 10 or mastery_gap > 40:
        return 0.0

    # Prefer peers that share the same curriculum segment (helps perceived achievability)
    path_overlap = len(set(user["curriculum_path"]) & set(peer["curriculum_path"])) / len(user["curriculum_path"])
    # Boost if user confidence is already high → they can handle a stretch target
    confidence_factor = 0.5 + 0.5 * user["confidence"]   # 0.5‑1.0

    return mastery_gap * path_overlap * confidence_factor


def _relatability_score(user: EmotionalState, peer: PeerProfile) -> float:
    """
    Higher when the peer is *near‑level* and has a recent success story that mirrors the user’s difficulty.
    """
    # Near‑level gap: within ±5 points of recent_score
    score_gap = abs(user["recent_score"] - peer["recent_score"])
    if score_gap > 5:
        return 0.0

    # Prefer peers who previously logged a high frustration but then improved
    improvement_factor = max(0.0, peer["recent_score"] - peer["previous_score"])
    # Weight by user frustration (more frustrated → need stronger relatability)
    frustration_factor = 0.5 + 0.5 * user["frustration"]   # 0.5‑1.0

    return (5 - score_gap) * (1 + improvement_factor) * frustration_factor
```

## 3️⃣ Core selection routine

```python
import random
import math
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional

def select_peer_for_motivation(
    current_user_id: str,
    user_emotional_state: EmotionalState,
    peer_database: List[PeerProfile],
) -> Tuple[Optional[PeerProfile], str]:
    """
    Returns a tuple (peer_profile_or_None, strategy_used).

    The function follows this high‑level flow:
        1️⃣  Decide which strategy (Aspiration vs Relatability) best fits the
            learner’s current affective profile.
        2️⃣  Score every consented peer according to the chosen strategy.
        3️⃣  Apply a *soft* similarity filter to keep the comparison believable.
        4️⃣  Sample probabilistically from the top‑k candidates (adds variety
            while still being purposeful).
        5️⃣  If no suitable peer is found, fall back to a *generic* motivational
            message (never return None to the UI layer).
    """
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 0️⃣  Quick sanity guard – make sure we have consented peers
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    consented_peers = [p for p in peer_database if p["consent_to_compare"]]
    if not consented_peers:
        return None, "fallback"

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Choose strategy based on emotional cues
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Rough heuristic (tune thresholds with A/B testing)
    if user_emotional_state["confidence"] > 0.7 and user_emotional_state["engagement"] > 0.6:
        # Learner is comfortable → give them an *ambitious* target
        chosen_strategy = "aspiration"
    elif user_emotional_state["frustration"] > 0.5 or user_emotional_state["confidence"] < 0.4:
        # Learner is struggling → give them a *relatable* story
        chosen_strategy = "relatability"
    else:
        # Mixed signals → pick the higher‑impact one (weighted random)
        chosen_strategy = random.choices(
            ["aspiration", "relatability"], weights=[0.45, 0.55], k=1
        )[0]

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Score peers according to the chosen strategy
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    scored_peers: List[Tuple[PeerProfile, float]] = []
    for peer in consented_peers:
        # Base similarity filter – we never want a completely foreign comparison
        sim = _similarity(user_emotional_state, peer)
        if sim < 0.3:          # discard peers that are too dissimilar
            continue

        if chosen_strategy == "aspiration":
            raw = _aspiration_score(user_emotional_state, peer)
        else:  # relatability
            raw = _relatability_score(user_emotional_state, peer)

        # Blend raw strategy score with similarity (makes the final rank smoother)
        final_score = raw * 0.8 + sim * 0.2
        if final_score > 0:
            scored_peers.append((peer, final_score))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  If no candidate survived → switch strategy (fallback)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    if not scored_peers:
        # Try the opposite strategy once
        alt_strategy = "relatability" if chosen_strategy == "aspiration" else "aspiration"
        for peer in consented_peers:
            sim = _similarity(user_emotional_state, peer)
            if sim < 0.3:
                continue
            raw = _aspiration_score(user_emotional_state, peer) if alt_strategy == "aspiration" else _relatability_score(user_emotional_state, peer)
            final_score = raw * 0.8 + sim * 0.2
            if final_score > 0:
                scored_peers.append((peer, final_score))
        if scored_peers:
            chosen_strategy = alt_strategy

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Pick from the top‑k (adds variety while staying purposeful)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    if scored_peers:
        # Sort descending by score
        scored_peers.sort(key=lambda tup: tup[1], reverse=True)
        top_k = scored_peers[:min(5, len(scored_peers))]   # usually 3‑5 candidates

        # Probabilistic draw: higher scores get proportionally higher chance
        total = sum(score for _, score in top_k)
        r = random.random() * total
        cumulative = 0.0
        for peer, score in top_k:
            cumulative += score
            if r <= cumulative:
                return peer, chosen_strategy

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Final fallback – return a generic, non‑personalized “motivational tip”
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    return None, "fallback"
```

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# focus_guardian.py
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Purpose
# -------
#   Detect when a learner is about to (or already) look for
#   external help – e.g. switching windows, opening a search engine,
#   copying the exact problem statement, or pasting a known‑answer URL.
#   When this happens we intervene *immediately* with a constructive
#   in‑system action (scaffolding hint, peer‑relatability nudge, etc.)
#
#   The function returns a tiny decision object that the caller
#   can log and/or use to trigger a UI overlay.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, Any, NamedTuple
import datetime as dt
import re

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣  Possible interventions (expand as your product grows)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
class GuardianIntervention(Enum):
    NONE                 = "none"
    SCAFFOLDING_HINT    = "scaffolding_hint"
    RELATABLE_PEER       = "relatable_peer"
    MINOR_BREAK          = "micro_break"
    MOTIVATIONAL_NUDGE   = "motivational_nudge"


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣  Decision payload (easy to serialize & log)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
class GuardianDecision(NamedTuple):
    intervention: GuardianIntervention
    confidence:   float            # 0‑1 – how sure we are that help‑seeking is occurring
    reason:       str              # human‑readable justification (for analytics)
    payload:      Dict[str, Any]   # optional extra data (e.g. hint ID, peer profile)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣  Helper: simple URL classifier – detects search engines,
#     Q&A sites, or known answer‑pages.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
_SEARCH_REGEX = re.compile(
    r"(https?://)?(www\.)?"
    r"(google|bing|duckduckgo|yahoo|baidu|ask)\.(com|org|cn|co\.uk)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_QA_REGEX = re.compile(
    r"(https?://)?(www\.)?"
    r"(stackoverflow\.com|stackexchange\.com|quora\.com|chegg\.com|coursehero\.com|brainly\.com)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

def _is_search_engine(url: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_SEARCH_REGEX.search(url))


def _is_known_qa_site(url: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_QA_REGEX.search(url))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 4️⃣  Helper: detect if clipboard contains the exact problem text.
#     (The tutor stores a short hash of the current problem; we
#     compare against it.  Use a fuzzy match to tolerate extra whitespace.)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
def _clipboard_matches_problem(clipboard: str, problem_hash: str) -> bool:
    """
    `problem_hash` is a short SHA‑256 (or similar) fingerprint that the
    front‑end computed from the problem statement when the user opened it.
    For speed we compare the *first 8 characters* of the hash.
    """
    if not clipboard:
        return False
    # Very cheap fingerprint – take the first 8 chars of an MD5 of the text.
    # In production you would compute the hash once on the client and
    # send the short token together with activity_data.
    import hashlib
    clipped_hash = hashlib.md5(clipboard.encode("utf‑8")).hexdigest()[:8]
    return clipped_hash == problem_hash[:8]

# 5️⃣  Core routine – decides whether to intervene
# -----------------------------------------------------------------

    user_id: str,

    """
    Parameters
    ----------
    user_id : str
        Opaque identifier – never logged with PII.

    activity_data : dict

            "alt_tab_count": int,                # how many times user switched away

            "current_problem_hash": str,         # short fingerprint of the active problem
            "last_intervention": {
                "type": str,
                "timestamp": datetime,
            },

    """

    new_tab_url        = activity_data.get("new_browser_tab_url", "")

                intervention=GuardianIntervention.NONE,
                confidence=0.0,
                reason="cool‑down active",
                payload={}
            )

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # c) Heuristic flags – each contributes to an overall risk score (0‑1)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    risk_score = 0.0
    reasons    = []          # for debugging / analytics

    #   • 0‑2 tabs   → low risk
    #   • 3‑5 tabs  → moderate risk
    #   • >5 tabs   → high risk

    # ---- 2. Opening a search engine or Q&A site -------------------------------

            reasons.append(f"search_engine_url={new_tab_url}")
        elif _is_known_qa_site(new_tab_url):

        # into an external search box.

        reasons.append("clipboard_matches_current_problem")

    # ---- 4. Low confidence / high frustration (from emotional model) ---------
    confidence = tutor_state.get("confidence", 0.5)   # 0‑1 where 1 = very confident

        reasons.append(f"low_confidence={confidence:.2f}")

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # d) Clamp final risk between 0‑1
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    risk_score = max(0.0, min(1.0, risk_score))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # e) Decision logic – map risk_score to concrete intervention
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    #   * ≥0.70     : Show a relatable‑peer success story + hint
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    if risk_score < 0.25:
        decision = GuardianDecision(
            intervention=GuardianIntervention.NONE,
            confidence=risk_score,
            reason="risk below threshold",
            payload={}
        )

    elif risk_score < 0.45:
        decision = GuardianDecision(
            intervention=GuardianIntervention.MOTIVATIONAL_NUDGE,
            confidence=risk_score,
            reason="moderate risk – gentle reminder",
            payload={"text": "Take a breath and give it another try – you’ve got this!"}
        )

    elif risk_score < 0.70:
        # Immediate scaffolding hint – we call the hint‑engine here
        hint_id = trigger_scaffolding_hint(user_id, tutor_state)
        decision = GuardianDecision(
            intervention=GuardianIntervention.SCAFFOLDING_HINT,
            confidence=risk_score,
            reason="high risk – provide in‑system hint",
            payload={"hint_id": hint_id}
        )

    else:
        # Very high risk (clipboard copy + search) → launch relatability peer
        peer, _ = select_peer_for_motivation(
            user_id,
            tutor_state.get("emotional_state", {}),
            peer_database=load_peer_database()   # abstracted helper
        )
        if peer:
            decision = GuardianDecision(
                intervention=GuardianIntervention.RELATABLE_PEER,
                confidence=risk_score,
                reason="critical risk – show relatable peer + hint",
                payload={
                    "peer_id": peer["peer_id"],
                    "display_name": peer["display_name"],
                    "story": peer.get("last_success_story", "")
                }
            )
        else:
            # Fallback if no peer is available
            decision = GuardianDecision(
                intervention=GuardianIntervention.SCAFFOLDING_HINT,
                confidence=risk_score,
                reason="critical risk – no peer, fallback to hint",
                payload={"hint_id": trigger_scaffolding_hint(user_id, tutor_state)}
            )

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # f) Record the decision (for analytics & cool‑down enforcement)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    _log_guardian_decision(
        user_id=user_id,
        decision=decision,
        activity_snapshot=activity_data,
        tutor_state_snapshot=tutor_state
    )
    # Also update the tutor_state so the next call knows we just intervened
    tutor_state["last_intervention"] = {
        "type": decision.intervention.value,
        "timestamp": now
    }

    return decision
```

|--------------------|----------------|------------------------|

| **Low confidence + any of the above** | The learner is vulnerable; a small nudge can keep them engaged. | Combine a *motivational message* with a *hint* or *peer* so the external temptation feels unnecessary. |
| **Repeated interventions within a short window** | Avoid “nagging” that could lead to disengagement. | Enforce a **2‑minute cool‑down** per user; after the cooldown the next high‑risk event will trigger again. |

### Safety / Ethical considerations (must be enforced)

* **Privacy** – Never log the *full* clipboard content or the *exact* URL unless the user explicitly opted‑in for “full‑trace” monitoring. Store only a **hash** or a **category** (e.g., `search_engine`, `qa_site`).

## High‑Level Flow

1. **Normalize** the incoming real‑time metrics (z‑score against the user’s own historical baseline).  
2. **Detect** a deviation that crosses a confidence‑threshold for each cue.  
3. **Fuse** the cues (simple weighted sum or a tiny classifier) to produce a *stress score* and a *positivity score*.  
4. **Lookup** the appropriate intervention from a rule table (or a tiny ML model).  
5. **Return** the selected intervention (or `None` if nothing fires).

```python
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional

def compute_z_score(value: float, mean: float, std: float) -> float:
    """Standard‑score relative to a user‑specific baseline."""
    if std == 0:        # avoid division‑by‑zero
        return 0.0
    return (value - mean) / std


def weighted_average(values: Dict[str, float], weights: Dict[str, float]) -> float:
    """Simple linear fusion of cues."""
    return sum(values[k] * weights.get(k, 0) for k in values) / sum(weights.values())


def get_user_baseline(user_id: str, metric: str, historical_data: Dict) -> (float, float):
    """
    Pull the mean and standard‑deviation for a specific metric
    from the user’s historical record.
    The `historical_data` argument is expected to be a dict like:
        {
            "typing_speed": {"mean": 250, "std": 50},
            "voice_pitch": {"mean": 200, "std": 30},
            "sentiment":   {"mean": 0.2, "std": 0.15},
            ...
        }
    """
    info = historical_data.get(metric, {})
    return info.get("mean", 0.0), info.get("std", 1.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------

def trigger_emotional_intervention(
    user_id: str,
    real_time_metrics: Dict[str, float],          # e.g. {"typing_speed": 180, "voice_pitch": 215, "sentiment": -0.45}
    historical_data:   Dict[str, Any]               # user‑specific baseline stats
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Decide which emotional‑support intervention to deploy.
    Returns one of:
        - "re_focus_prompt"
        - "motivational_boost"
        - "stress_relief_break"
        - None  (no action needed)
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Normalise each cue against the user’s own baseline
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    norm_metrics = {}
    for metric_name, raw_value in real_time_metrics.items():
        mu, sigma = get_user_baseline(user_id, metric_name, historical_data)
        norm_metrics[metric_name] = compute_z_score(raw_value, mu, sigma)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Detect short‑term anomalies
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Thresholds can be tuned per‑metric; here we keep them simple.
    # Positive Z → higher-than-usual ; Negative Z → lower‑than‑usual.
    anomalies = {
        "slow_typing":   norm_metrics["typing_speed"] < -1.0,   # typing much slower than usual
        "fast_typing":   norm_metrics["typing_speed"] >  1.0,   # typing unusually fast (possible agitation)
        "low_pitch":     norm_metrics["voice_pitch"]  < -0.8,
        "high_pitch":    norm_metrics["voice_pitch"]  >  0.8,
        "neg_sentiment": norm_metrics["sentiment"]    < -0.75,
        "pos_sentiment": norm_metrics["sentiment"]    >  0.75,
    }

    # 3️⃣  Fuse cues into higher‑level scores
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A tiny handcrafted risk model – you could replace this with a logistic‑regression
    # trained on labeled sessions.
    stress_weights = {
        "slow_typing":   0.4,
        "fast_typing":   0.3,
        "low_pitch":     0.2,
        "high_pitch":    0.2,
        "neg_sentiment":0.5,
    }

        "fast_typing":   0.2,
        "high_pitch":    0.3,
        "pos_sentiment":0.5,

        {k: int(v) for k, v in anomalies.items()},
        positivity_weights
    )
```

```python
    return peer.get("opt_in_peer_compare", False)

def recent_activity_score(peer: Dict[str, Any], days_limit: int = 7) -> float:
    """Penalise peers that haven’t been active lately."""
    # In a real system you would parse dates; here we assume a numeric “days_ago”.
    days_ago = peer.get("days_since_last_activity", 0)
    return clamp(1 - days_ago / days_limit)   # 1 = today, 0 = >limit days old
```

## 3️⃣ Core scoring functions

### 3.1 Aspiration‑Target score  
Aims to pick a *slightly better* learner.

```python
def aspiration_score(
    learner_mastery: float,
    learner_speed:   float,
    peer: Dict[str, Any],
    mastery_gap_max: float = 0.15,   # 15 % ahead is still reachable
    mastery_gap_min: float = 0.05    # at least 5 % ahead to feel aspirational
) -> float:
    """
    Higher score = peer is a good aspiration target.
    """
    if not is_eligible(peer):
        return 0.0

    peer_mastery = peer["mastery"]
    peer_speed   = peer.get("speed", 1.0)

    # 1) Must be ahead, but not too far
    gap = signed_distance(peer_mastery, learner_mastery)
    if gap < mastery_gap_min or gap > mastery_gap_max:
        return 0.0

    # 2) Prefer peers that are faster (shows efficiency)
    speed_factor = clamp(peer_speed / learner_speed)  # >1 => quicker

    # 3) Recent activity matters
    activity_factor = recent_activity_score(peer)

    # 4) Emotional tone – we want a *positive* peer (high sentiment, low stress)
    sentiment = peer.get("recent_sentiment", 0.0)      # range ≈ [-1, 1]
    stress    = peer.get("recent_stress", 0.0)         # range [0, 1]
    emotion_factor = clamp((sentiment + 1) / 2) * (1 - stress)

    # 5) Combine – weighted geometric mean (prevents any single zero from killing everything)
    #    weights can be tuned via A/B testing.
    w_gap       = 0.35
    w_speed     = 0.20
    w_activity  = 0.15
    w_emotion   = 0.30

    # Normalise gap to [0,1] where 0 = min‑gap, 1 = max‑gap
    norm_gap = (gap - mastery_gap_min) / (mastery_gap_max - mastery_gap_min)

    # Geometric blend (multiplicative) keeps the score low if any factor is low.
    score = (
        (norm_gap ** w_gap) *
        (speed_factor ** w_speed) *
        (activity_factor ** w_activity) *
        (emotion_factor ** w_emotion)
    )
    return clamp(score)
```

### 3.2 Relatability‑Target score  
Finds a peer *near the learner* who is doing well emotionally.

```python
def relatability_score(
    learner_mastery: float,
    learner_speed:   float,
    peer: Dict[str, Any],
    mastery_tolerance: float = 0.05   # ±5 % mastery tolerance
) -> float:
    """
    Higher score = peer is a good relatability target.
    """
    if not is_eligible(peer):
        return 0.0

    peer_mastery = peer["mastery"]
    peer_speed   = peer.get("speed", 1.0)

    # 1) Mastery must be within tolerance (both slightly higher or slightly lower)
    diff = signed_distance(peer_mastery, learner_mastery)
    if abs(diff) > mastery_tolerance:
        return 0.0

    # 2) Prefer peers that are *slightly* ahead (so the learner can see a reachable improvement)
    #    but also treat slightly‑behind peers as okay if their emotional tone is excellent.
    mastery_factor = 0.5 + 0.5 * math.tanh(diff / mastery_tolerance)   # maps [-tol,+tol] → [0,1]

    # 3) Speed similarity – we want the learner to think “they are on a comparable pace”
    speed_similarity = 1 - abs(peer_speed - learner_speed) / max(learner_speed, peer_speed)

    # 4) Emotional tone – this is the *core* for relatability.
    sentiment = peer.get("recent_sentiment", 0.0)      # [-1, 1]
    stress    = peer.get("recent_stress", 0.0)         # [0, 1]
    # Positive sentiment and low stress are ideal.
    emotion_factor = clamp((sentiment + 1) / 2) * (1 - stress)

    # 5) Recent activity – still important
    activity_factor = recent_activity_score(peer)

    # 6) Weighted blend (linear this time – relatability is more tolerant)
    w_mastery   = 0.30
    w_speed     = 0.20
    w_emotion   = 0.35
    w_activity  = 0.15

    score = (
        mastery_factor   * w_mastery   +
        speed_similarity * w_speed    +
        emotion_factor   * w_emotion  +
        activity_factor  * w_activity
    )
    return clamp(score)
```

## 4️⃣ Main selection routine

```python
def select_peer_for_motivation(
    current_user_id: str,
    user_emotional_state: Dict[str, float],
    peer_database: List[Dict[str, Any]]
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Returns a *single* peer record (or None if no suitable peer is found).
    The returned dict can be fed directly to the UI layer for rendering.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4.1 Load current learner’s latest performance snapshot.
    # (In practice you would query a fast cache / feature store.)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    learner_snapshot = get_latest_user_snapshot(current_user_id)   # see note below
    learner_mastery = learner_snapshot["mastery"]                 # 0‑1 on the current lesson
    learner_speed   = learner_snapshot.get("speed", 1.0)           # relative speed factor

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4.2 Decide which *motivation* strategy to employ.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    confidence = user_emotional_state.get("confidence", 0.0)   # negative = frustrated
    stress     = user_emotional_state.get("stress", 0.0)       # 0‑1

    # Simple rule‑based switch (tune thresholds via experiments):
    #   • If confidence is *moderately high* or the user shows *curiosity* → Aspiration.
    #   • If confidence is low or stress is high → Relatability.
    ASPIRATION_CONFIDENCE_MIN = 0.10   # e.g., user feels at least a little upbeat
    STRESS_THRESHOLD          = 0.55

    use_aspiration = (confidence >= ASPIRATION_CONFIDENCE_MIN) and (stress < STRESS_THRESHOLD)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4.3 Score all peers with the appropriate function.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    best_peer: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    best_score = -1.0

    for peer in peer_database:
        # Skip self‑comparison
        if peer["peer_id"] == current_user_id:
            continue

        if use_aspiration:
            score = aspiration_score(
                learner_mastery,
                learner_speed,
                peer,
                mastery_gap_min=0.05,
                mastery_gap_max=0.15
            )
        else:
            score = relatability_score(
                learner_mastery,
                learner_speed,
                peer,
                mastery_tolerance=0.05
            )

        # Small random jitter (0‑5 %) to avoid the *same* peer every time when scores tie.
        jitter = random.uniform(0.95, 1.05)
        score *= jitter

        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best_peer = peer

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4.4 If no peer passes the eligibility / score filter, fall back to a neutral placeholder.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    SCORE_CUTOFF = 0.12          # empirically chosen; lower => too many weak matches
    if best_peer is None or best_score < SCORE_CUTOFF:
        return None   # UI can render “Your progress is unique – keep it up!” or a generic tip.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4.5 Attach a *reason tag* (useful for analytics & A/B testing)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    best_peer = best_peer.copy()   # avoid mutating the DB record
    best_peer["motivation_strategy"] = "aspiration" if use_aspiration else "relatability"
    best_peer["motivation_score"]    = round(best_score, 3)

    return best_peer
```

## 5️⃣ Why this logic stays **constructive**  

| Risk | How the code mitigates it |
|------|---------------------------|
| **Comparing to an unreachable “super‑star”** | Aspiration targets are limited to a *max* mastery gap (default 15 %). |
| **Showing a peer who is actually worse** | Relatability targets require the peer to be within ±5 % mastery *and* emotionally positive. |
| **Repeating the same peer (annoyance)** | Random jitter + the *score‑cutoff* ensure a broad pool is used; you can also add a “recently shown” blacklist (e.g., exclude peers shown in the last N cards). |
| **Negative emotional contagion** | Both scores heavily weight **low stress / high sentiment**; a stressed peer will get a near‑zero score. |
| **Privacy / consent violation** | Every peer must have `opt_in_peer_compare == True`. You can also filter by demographic similarity if you want to hide identity details. |

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Pseudocode: Emotional‑Intervention Trigger for a Tutoring AI
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Input:
#   user_id               – unique identifier of the learner
#   real_time_metrics     – dict with latest sensor/interaction data
#        {
#           "typing_speed"   : float (chars per second),
#           "voice_pitch"    : float (Hz, optional – only if voice is used),
#           "sentiment"      : float (‑1.0 … 1.0, from a sentiment analyzer),
#           "engagement"     : float (0‑1, e.g. gaze‑fixation, mouse activity)
#        }
#   historical_data       – pre‑computed profile for the learner
#        {
#           "baseline_typing_speed" : float,
#           "baseline_sentiment"    : float,
#           "stress_history"        : list[float]  # recent sentiment values
#           "preferred_interventions": ["visual‑hint", "encouragement", …],
#           "intervention_cooldown" : int (seconds since last trigger)
#        }
#
# Output:
#   dict with the chosen intervention (or None)
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def trigger_emotional_intervention(user_id, real_time_metrics, historical_data):
    """
    Decide whether an emotional‑support intervention is needed,
    and if so, which one best fits the learner's current state
    and long‑term preferences.
    """

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Normalise / compute delta values relative to the learner’s baseline
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    dt_typing   = real_time_metrics["typing_speed"] - historical_data["baseline_typing_speed"]
    dt_sentiment = real_time_metrics["sentiment"] - historical_data["baseline_sentiment"]
    engagement   = real_time_metrics["engagement"]

    # Simple “stress flag” – negative sentiment combined with slower typing
    stress_score = (-dt_sentiment) * 0.6 + (-dt_typing) * 0.4   # weights can be tuned
    stress_score = max(0.0, min(stress_score, 1.0))            # clamp to 0‑1

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Look at recent trend (last N sentiment points) to avoid reacting
    #     to a single blip.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    recent_trend = compute_recent_sentiment_trend(historical_data["stress_history"])
    # recent_trend returns a value in ‑1 … 1 (negative = deteriorating)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  Cool‑down check – do not spam the learner with interventions
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    if time_since_last_intervention(user_id) < historical_data["intervention_cooldown"]:
        return {"intervention": None, "reason": "cool‑down"}

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Decision tree / rule‑based gating
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4a) High stress & low engagement → “re‑engage” intervention
    if stress_score > 0.65 and engagement < 0.4:
        chosen = pick_intervention(
            candidate_list=["encouragement‑audio",
                            "quick‑breathing‑exercise",
                            "visual‑relax‑animation"],
            preferences=historical_data["preferred_interventions"]
        )
        reason = "high stress + low engagement"

    # 4b) Moderate stress but negative trend → “clarify” intervention
    elif stress_score > 0.40 and recent_trend < -0.2:
        chosen = pick_intervention(
            candidate_list=["concept‑reminder‑visual",
                            "step‑by‑step‑hint",
                            "mini‑quiz‑warm‑up"],
            preferences=historical_data["preferred_interventions"]
        )
        reason = "moderate stress + worsening sentiment"

    # 4c) Sudden drop in typing speed (possible frustration) → “break” cue
    elif dt_typing < -0.30 * historical_data["baseline_typing_speed"]:
        chosen = pick_intervention(
            candidate_list=["short‑break‑timer",
                            "light‑humor‑gif",
                            "stretch‑reminder"],
            preferences=historical_data["preferred_interventions"]
        )
        reason = "typing slowdown ≈ frustration"

    # 4d) Otherwise – no urgent emotional need
    else:
        return {"intervention": None, "reason": "no trigger"}

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Record the trigger (for cooldown & analytics)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    log_intervention(user_id, chosen, stress_score, engagement, dt_sentiment, dt_typing)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6️⃣  Return the selected intervention payload
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    return {
        "intervention" : chosen,                # e.g. "encouragement‑audio"
        "payload"      : build_payload(chosen), # URLs, text, audio files, etc.
        "reason"       : reason,
        "metrics"      : {
            "stress_score" : stress_score,
            "engagement"   : engagement,
            "dt_sentiment" : dt_sentiment,
            "dt_typing"    : dt_typing
        }
    }


# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper utilities (still pseudocode – implement with your tech stack)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
def compute_recent_sentiment_trend(history, window=5):
    """Return slope‑like trend over the last `window` entries."""
    if len(history) < window:
        return 0.0
    recent = history[-window:]
    # simple linear regression on indices vs sentiment
    return linear_regression_slope(range(window), recent)

def pick_intervention(candidate_list, preferences):
    """
    Prefer interventions the learner has liked before.
    If none match, fall back to a random choice weighted by generic effectiveness.
    """
    # keep order of preferences but filter out unavailable ones
    preferred = [c for c in preferences if c in candidate_list]
    if preferred:
        return preferred[0]                     # highest‑ranked preferred type
    # otherwise weighted random (weights could come from A/B test data)
    return weighted_random_choice(candidate_list)

def time_since_last_intervention(user_id):
    """Query your logs / cache for the timestamp of the last trigger."""
    last_ts = get_last_intervention_ts(user_id)
    return now() - last_ts                       # seconds

def log_intervention(user_id, kind, *args):
    """Persist the event for cooldown handling and analytics."""
    save_to_db({
        "user_id"      : user_id,
        "intervention" : kind,
        "timestamp"    : now(),
        "details"      : args
    })

def build_payload(kind):
    """Map an intervention identifier to the actual content to deliver."""
    mapping = {
        "encouragement-audio"   : {"type":"audio", "url":"/assets/encourage.mp3"},
        "quick-breathing-exercise": {"type":"script", "steps":["inhale 4s","hold 4s","exhale 4s"]},
        "visual-relax-animation": {"type":"video", "url":"/assets/relax.mp4"},
        "concept-reminder-visual": {"type":"image", "url":"/assets/reminder.png"},
        "step-by-step-hint"      : {"type":"text", "message":"Try breaking the equation into…"},
        "mini-quiz-warm-up"      : {"type":"quiz", "questions":load_quiz("warmup")},
        "short-break-timer"      : {"type":"timer", "duration":120},
        "light-humor-gif"        : {"type":"gif", "url":"/assets/funny.gif"},
        "stretch-reminder"       : {"type":"text", "message":"Stand up and stretch for 30 s!"}
    }
    return mapping.get(kind, {})
```

| Step | What it achieves | Why it matters for “Indispensable” learning |
|------|------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| **Normalise vs. baseline** | Detects deviations that are *personal* to each learner (slow typing for a fast typist is a bigger red‑flag). | The tutor feels “in‑tune” with the individual, not generic. |
| **Trend analysis** | Looks at the **direction** of sentiment, avoiding over‑reacting to one‑off spikes. | Learners experience interventions only when truly needed, preventing annoyance. |
| **Cooldown** | Guarantees a minimum gap between emotional nudges. | Keeps the tutor trustworthy—students won’t feel “spammed”. |
| **Rule‑based gating** | Maps concrete behavioural signatures (stress + low engagement, slowing typing, etc.) to a **catalog of support actions**. | Each trigger leads to a concrete, helpful next step, reinforcing the habit “when I’m stuck, the tutor helps me right away”. |
| **Preference‑aware selection** | Uses the learner’s historic “liked” interventions first, then falls back to evidence‑based defaults. | The assistance feels *personalised* and respects the student’s own style. |
| **Logging & analytics** | Stores every decision for later refinement (e.g., reinforcement‑learning upgrades). | Continuous improvement ensures the tutor stays ahead of the learner’s evolving needs, cementing long‑term dependency. |

Feel free to replace the simple rule‑based logic with a learned classifier (e.g., a lightweight Gradient Boosting model) once you have enough logged interactions. The overall scaffold above will remain the same – just the decision engine inside the `if/elif` block would be swapped for a model‑prediction call.

## 2️⃣  Core selection function

```python
import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def select_peer_for_motivation(current_user_id,
                               user_emotional_state,
                               peer_database):
    """
    Return a *single* peer record (or None) that will be displayed to the
    current learner as a social‑comparison benchmark.
    The choice follows two complementary strategies:
        1️⃣ Aspiration Target  – a slightly higher‑performing peer.
        2️⃣ Relatability Target – a peer whose metrics are close to the learner’s.
    """
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.1  Load the current learner’s own performance profile
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    learner_profile = fetch_user_profile(current_user_id)   # from your DB
    learner_perf   = learner_profile["performance_score"]
    learner_progress = learner_profile["recent_progress"]
    learner_engage   = learner_profile["engagement_score"]
    learner_sentiment = learner_profile["sentiment_score"]

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.2  Decide WHICH STRATEGY to use (based on emotional state)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # Simple heuristic – you can replace it with a small ML model later.
    #   *high confidence* → Aspiration
    #   *low confidence / stress* → Relatability
    sentiment   = user_emotional_state["sentiment"]
    stress      = user_emotional_state["stress_index"]
    typing_speed_delta = user_emotional_state["typing_speed"] - learner_profile["baseline_typing_speed"]
    engagement  = user_emotional_state["engagement"]

    # ---- Decision rule ----
    if (sentiment > 0.3 and stress < 0.3 and typing_speed_delta > 0):
        strategy = "aspiration"
    else:
        strategy = "relatability"

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.3  Filter peers that we are allowed to show
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    now = datetime.utcnow()
    eligible_peers = [
        p for p in peer_database
        if p["consent_to_share"]
        and (now - p["last_active"]).days <= 30          # active enough
        and p["peer_id"] != current_user_id               # never self‑compare
    ]

    if not eligible_peers:
        return None      # fallback – no peer shown

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.4  Helper: score how well a peer matches a given strategy
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    def aspiration_score(peer):
        """
        Prefer:
          • performance just above learner (but not too far)
          • visible recent progress (shows momentum)
          • positive sentiment (inspirational tone)
        """
        perf_gap   = peer["performance_score"] - learner_perf
        # We want a gap in a sweet‑spot 5‑15 % above learner
        gap_score  = max(0, 1 - abs(perf_gap - 0.10) / 0.10)   # 1 at 10 % gap
        prog_score = peer["recent_progress"]                # higher = better
        senti_score= (peer["sentiment_score"] + 1) / 2      # 0‑1 scale
        # Weighted sum (tune weights later)
        return 0.5 * gap_score + 0.3 * prog_score + 0.2 * senti_score

    def relatability_score(peer):
        """
        Prefer peers that look *almost identical* to the learner:
          • performance within ±5 %
          • similar engagement
          • similar sentiment
        """
        perf_diff  = abs(peer["performance_score"] - learner_perf)
        engg_diff  = abs(peer["engagement_score"] - learner_engage)
        sent_diff  = abs(peer["sentiment_score"] - learner_sentiment)

        # Inverse distance – smaller diff → higher score
        perf_score = max(0, 1 - perf_diff / 0.05)   # 0‑1
        engg_score = max(0, 1 - engg_diff / 0.10)   # allow a bit larger window
        sent_score = max(0, 1 - sent_diff / 0.15)

        # Small boost for recent progress (makes the peer look “alive”)
        prog_bonus = 0.1 * peer["recent_progress"]

        return 0.4 * perf_score + 0.3 * engg_score + 0.2 * sent_score + prog_bonus

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.5  Rank peers according to the selected strategy
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if strategy == "aspiration":
        scored = [(aspiration_score(p), p) for p in eligible_peers]
    else:   # relatability
        scored = [(relatability_score(p), p) for p in eligible_peers]

    # Sort descending by score
    scored.sort(key=lambda tup: tup[0], reverse=True)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.6  Choose the top‑N candidates and add a tiny randomization step
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    TOP_N = 5
    top_candidates = [p for score, p in scored[:TOP_N] if score > 0]

    if not top_candidates:
        return None       # no peer passes the score threshold

    # Randomly pick one from the elite bucket – this avoids the same
    # peer being shown every single time while preserving the intended
    # motivational direction.
    chosen_peer = random.choice(top_candidates)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.7  Build the *public* representation that will be sent to the UI
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    public_handle = anonymize_handle(chosen_peer["peer_id"])   # e.g., "Alex 🚀"
    return {
        "peer_id"          : chosen_peer["peer_id"],   # keep internal for logging
        "display_name"     : public_handle,
        "performance_score": round(chosen_peer["performance_score"], 2),
        "recent_progress" : round(chosen_peer["recent_progress"], 2),
        "sentiment_score" : round(chosen_peer["sentiment_score"], 2),
        "strategy_used"   : strategy,
        "rationale"       : (
            "aspiration" if strategy == "aspiration"
            else "relatability"
        )
    }
```

### 3️⃣  Why each piece matters for a **constructive** peer‑comparison loop

| Block | Constructive‑Motivation Mechanism |
|-------|-----------------------------------|
| **Emotional‑state decision** | Uses live sentiment & stress to pick a tone that matches the learner’s current mood (ambitious vs. reassuring). |
| **Eligibility filter** | Guarantees freshness, consent, and anonymity – essential for ethical social comparison. |
| **Aspiration scoring** | Creates a *reachable* “next rung” (≈10 % performance gap). Too large a gap would feel demotivating; too small a gap would feel meaningless. |
| **Relatability scoring** | Finds a peer whose numbers are almost identical, delivering the “someone just like me did it” effect that lowers perceived difficulty. |
| **Top‑N + random pick** | Prevents the same peer from appearing over‑and‑over (reduces envy or fatigue) while still keeping the motivational direction intact. |
| **Public payload** | Sends only aggregated numbers and an anonymous handle, protecting privacy while still providing a vivid benchmark. |
| **Logging (not shown but assumed)** | Every selection is logged with the learner’s emotional state, so you can later audit that the system is *always* choosing constructive peers and adjust thresholds if needed. |

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Focus Guardian – Detect & pre‑empt external‑help seeking
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# INPUTS
#   user_id          : str   – unique learner identifier
#   activity_data   : dict  – realtime UI / OS telemetry
#       {
#           "alt_tab_count"        : int,      # #times user switched windows in last N seconds
#           "new_browser_tab_url"  : str|None, # URL of a newly‑opened tab (None if no new tab)
#           "clipboard_content"    : str|None, # text currently on the clipboard (None if unchanged)
#           "timestamp"            : datetime   # when the snapshot was taken
#       }
#   tutor_state      : dict  – current internal state of the tutoring session
#       {
#           "current_topic"        : str,
#           "last_scaffold_time"   : datetime,
#           "last_peer_offer_time" : datetime,
#           "cooldown_seconds"     : int,     # minimum gap between any focus‑guardian intervention
#           "problem_text"         : str,     # the exact statement the learner is working on
#           "session_id"           : str,
#       }
#
# RETURNS
#   dict with the chosen intervention (or None) and a short reason
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def intercept_external_help_seeking(user_id, activity_data, tutor_state):
    """
    Detect a probable external‑help request and inject a native
    intervention (scaffolding hint or relatability‑peer offer) before
    the learner can disengage.
    """

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Quick‑exit / “help‑seeking” heuristics
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    #   • Alt‑Tab burst → user switching away repeatedly
    #   • New browser tab that looks like a search engine / Q&A site
    #   • Clipboard contains the exact problem text (or a large fragment)
    #
    #   Each signal gets a score; if the total exceeds a threshold we act.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    # ---- a) Alt‑Tab detection -------------------------------------------------
    ALT_TAB_WINDOW_SECONDS = 30          # look‑back window for the count
    ALT_TAB_THRESHOLD      = 3           # > 3 switches in the window = suspicious
    alt_tab_score = 0
    if activity_data["alt_tab_count"] >= ALT_TAB_THRESHOLD:
        alt_tab_score = 0.4               # weight for rapid window‑switching

    # ---- b) New browser tab detection -----------------------------------------
    # We only care about *new* tabs that appear while the tutor UI is focused.
    # If the URL contains known “search/help” domains we raise the flag.
    SEARCH_DOMAINS = ["google.", "bing.", "duckduckgo.", "yahoo.", "baidu.",
                     "stackexchange.", "stackoverflow.", "reddit.", "khanacademy.",
                     "chegg.", "coursehero.", "answers.yahoo.", "quizlet."]
    browser_score = 0
    url = activity_data.get("new_browser_tab_url")
    if url:
        lowered = url.lower()
        if any(dom in lowered for dom in SEARCH_DOMAINS):
            browser_score = 0.5           # strongest single indicator

    # ---- c) Clipboard copy detection -------------------------------------------
    # If the learner copies *the exact problem text* (or >70% of it) we assume
    # they are about to paste it elsewhere (e.g., a search engine).
    clipboard_score = 0
    clip = activity_data.get("clipboard_content")
    if clip:
        # normalise both strings: lower case, strip whitespace
        problem = tutor_state["problem_text"].strip().lower()
        copied  = clip.strip().lower()

        # Simple similarity: Jaccard over word sets or a fuzzy ratio
        similarity = jaccard_similarity(problem, copied)      # 0‑1
        # or use a cheap Levenshtein ratio if you prefer
        # similarity = levenshtein_ratio(problem, copied)

        if similarity >= 0.7:               # 70 % overlap → likely a copy‑paste
            clipboard_score = 0.6

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Combine scores → overall “help‑seeking confidence”
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE = alt_tab_score + browser_score + clipboard_score   # max 1.5
    # Normalise to 0‑1 range for easier threshold handling
    HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE = min(HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE / 1.5, 1.0)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  Cool‑down guard – avoid spamming the user
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    now = activity_data["timestamp"]
    time_since_last = (now - tutor_state["last_scaffold_time"]).total_seconds()
    time_since_peer  = (now - tutor_state["last_peer_offer_time"]).total_seconds()
    if time_since_last < tutor_state["cooldown_seconds"] and \
       time_since_peer  < tutor_state["cooldown_seconds"]:
        # Both interventions are still cooling down → do nothing
        return {"intervention": None, "reason": "cool‑down"}

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Decide which native intervention to fire
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    #   *If the clipboard copy is detected → give a direct scaffold (most urgent)*
    #   *If a search‑engine tab appears → offer a Relatability‑Target peer (social cue)*
    #   *If only Alt‑Tab bursts → a gentle “stay‑in‑flow” reminder*
    #
    #   We also make sure we do not repeat the exact same intervention
    #   within the current cooldown window.

    if clipboard_score > 0:                     # strongest signal → scaffolding hint
        # Build a brief, context‑aware hint (could be a micro‑video,
        # a textual “step‑by‑step” or a quick example)
        hint = generate_scaffold_hint(tutor_state["current_topic"])
        # Log for analytics / cooldown handling
        log_intervention(user_id, "scaffold_hint", now, HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE)

        # Update tutor_state timestamps for future cooldown checks
        tutor_state["last_scaffold_time"] = now

        return {
            "intervention" : "scaffold_hint",
            "payload"      : hint,
            "reason"       : "clipboard copy detected",
            "confidence"   : HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE
        }

    elif browser_score > 0:                     # user opened a search/Q&A tab
        # Choose a relatable peer (see previous pseudocode)
        peer = select_peer_for_motivation(
                current_user_id=user_id,
                user_emotional_state=extract_emotional_snapshot(user_id),
                peer_database=get_active_peer_db()
               )
        if peer:
            # Offer a “Let’s solve this together – see how Alex handled something similar”
            offer = {
                "type"        : "relatable_peer_offer",
                "peer_handle" : peer["display_name"],
                "peer_perf"   : peer["performance_score"],
                "peer_progress": peer["recent_progress"]
            }
            log_intervention(user_id, "relatable_peer_offer", now, HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE)
            tutor_state["last_peer_offer_time"] = now

            return {
                "intervention" : "relatable_peer_offer",
                "payload"      : offer,
                "reason"       : "search‑engine tab opened",
                "confidence"   : HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE
            }

    elif alt_tab_score > 0:                     # frequent window switching
        # Gentle “stay‑in‑flow” nudge (audio‑clip, short tip)
        nudge = {
            "type"    : "focus_nudge",
            "message" : random.choice([
                "💡 Remember, the solution is just a step away!",
                "🔎 Keep the focus – you’ve made great progress already.",
                "🚀 Let’s finish this together before the next coffee break."
            ])
        }
        log_intervention(user_id, "focus_nudge", now, HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE)
        # update only the generic cooldown (reuse scaffold slot)
        tutor_state["last_scaffold_time"] = now

        return {
            "intervention" : "focus_nudge",
            "payload"      : nudge,
            "reason"       : "alt‑tab burst detected",
            "confidence"   : HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE
        }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  No strong external‑help pattern detected → stay silent
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    return {"intervention": None, "reason": "no trigger", "confidence": HELP_SEEK_CONFIDENCE}

def jaccard_similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    """Simple token‑set Jaccard (0‑1)."""
    set_a = set(a.split())
    set_b = set(b.split())
    if not set_a or not set_b:
        return 0.0
    return len(set_a & set_b) / len(set_a | set_b)


def generate_scaffold_hint(topic: str) -> dict:
    """
    Return a ready‑to‑display hint tailored to the current topic.
    The actual content can be a pre‑rendered micro‑video, a text
    example, or an interactive widget.
    """
    # Example stub – replace with your content‑lookup service
    hint_library = {
        "quadratic_equations": {
            "type": "text",
            "content": "Recall the shape of a parabola: a = 1 opens upward. Try factoring first..."
        },
        "photosynthesis": {
            "type": "gif",
            "url": "/assets/leaf.gif",
            "caption": "Step‑by‑step: Light → Chlorophyll → Glucose"
        },
        # … more topics …
    }
    return hint_library.get(topic, {"type": "text", "content": "Take a short breath and read the definition again."})


def log_intervention(user_id: str, kind: str, ts: datetime, confidence: float):
    """Persist a lightweight event for analytics & cooldown tracking."""

    audit = {

    save_event(audit)                              # placeholder


def extract_emotional_snapshot(user_id: str) -> dict:
    """Grab the most recent sentiment/typing‑speed snapshot for peer‑selection."""

    return get_latest_emotion_metrics(user_id)


def get_active_peer_db() -> list:
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------
#  trigger_emotional_intervention
# --------------------------------------------------------------
#  INPUTS
#      user_id            : unique identifier for the learner
#      real_time_metrics : dict with keys
#            - typing_speed   (tokens / sec)
#            - voice_pitch    (Hz)   # optional, if voice‑capture is enabled
#            - sentiment      (float in [-1, 1])
#      historical_data    : dict (or a lightweight object) that holds
#            - baseline_typing_speed
#            - baseline_sentiment
#            - recent_intervention_history (list of last N interventions)
#            - engagement_score (0‑100) – e.g., from longer‑term logs
#
#  OUTPUT
#      Returns the name of the intervention that was dispatched
#      (e.g., "micro_reward", "narrative_hook", "reflective_prompt")
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def trigger_emotional_intervention(user_id, real_time_metrics, historical_data):
    """
    Decide, in real‑time, which emotional boost to give the learner.
    The logic combines:
        • Deviation from personal baselines
        • Trend over the past few minutes
        • Long‑term engagement patterns
        • Cool‑down rules (don’t spam the same kind of boost)
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Load the learner’s profile (preferences, known strengths, etc.)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    profile = get_user_profile(user_id)          # e.g., {"prefers_visual":True, ...}
    now = current_timestamp()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Normalise the incoming signals relative to the learner’s own history
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #   - a % change is more meaningful than an absolute number because each
    #     student types at a different speed, speaks at a different pitch, etc.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    speed_norm   = (real_time_metrics["typing_speed"] -
                    historical_data["baseline_typing_speed"]) / \
                    max(1.0, historical_data["baseline_typing_speed"])

    sentiment_norm = real_time_metrics["sentiment"] - historical_data["baseline_sentiment"]
    pitch_norm   = None
    if "voice_pitch" in real_time_metrics:
        pitch_norm = (real_time_metrics["voice_pitch"] -
                      historical_data.get("baseline_voice_pitch", 0)) / \
                     max(1.0, historical_data.get("baseline_voice_pitch", 1))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  Compute a simple “affect intensity” score
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #   Positive values → likely bored/over‑confident  → need a challenge or story
    #   Negative values → likely frustrated / disengaged → need encouragement
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    affect_score = (
        -0.6 * speed_norm      # slower typing → possible struggle
        -0.4 * sentiment_norm # negative sentiment → frustration
    )
    if pitch_norm is not None:
        affect_score += -0.2 * pitch_norm   # lower pitch can signal low arousal

    # Scale to [-1, 1] for easier rule‑writing
    affect_score = max(-1.0, min(1.0, affect_score))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Look at recent intervention history to avoid repetition
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    recent = historical_data.get("recent_intervention_history", [])
    last_intervention = recent[-1] if recent else None
    last_time = recent[-1]["timestamp"] if recent else None

    # Cool‑down: do not fire the same type within the last 2‑3 minutes
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 150
    def can_use(intervention_name):
        for entry in recent[-5:]:          # examine the last few entries only
            if entry["name"] == intervention_name and \
               now - entry["timestamp"] < COOLDOWN_SECONDS:
                return False
        return True

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Decision rules – choose the most appropriate boost
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    #   The rules are ordered by priority (most urgent first).
    #   Feel free to replace them with a learned policy (e.g., a bandit model).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    chosen_intervention = None
    payload = {}                     # extra data needed by the UI layer

    # ---- 5.1  If the learner looks *stressed* → give quick encouragement ----
    if affect_score < -0.5 and can_use("micro_reward"):
        chosen_intervention = "micro_reward"
        payload = {
            "message": random.choice([
                "You’re doing great – keep it up!",
                "A tiny win: +1 point for perseverance!",
                "Hey, remember how far you’ve come!"
            ]),
            "badge": "Boost"                       # could trigger a visual badge
        }

    # ---- 5.2  If the learner is *bored/over‑confident* → inject story hook ----
    elif affect_score > 0.5 and can_use("narrative_hook"):
        chosen_intervention = "narrative_hook"
        # Pick a story segment that matches the current topic
        topic = profile.get("current_topic", "default")
        story = select_story_fragment(topic)   # e.g., return a short plot line
        payload = {
            "title": f"🔍 Next Challenge: {story['title']}",
            "snippet": story["teaser"],
            "unlock_reward": story["reward"]
        }

    # ---- 5.3  If the learner is *moderately disengaged* → reflective prompt ----
    elif -0.5 <= affect_score <= 0.5 and can_use("reflective_prompt"):
        chosen_intervention = "reflective_prompt"
        payload = {
            "question": random.choice([
                "What part of today’s lesson clicked for you?",
                "Is there anything you’d like to revisit before moving on?",
                "Which example helped you understand the concept best?"
            ])
        }

    # ---- 5.4  Fallback: gentle nudge (always allowed) -----------------------
    else:
        if can_use("gentle_nudge"):
            chosen_intervention = "gentle_nudge"
            payload = {
                "message": "Take a quick breath, then let’s keep going!",
                "animation": "breathing_circle"
            }
        else:
            # If everything is on cooldown, simply return None (no push)
            return None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
```
